Everything works. Here's the full picture of what was added and why each piece exists:

**`SortAlgorithmProvider`** (`sorting.core`) — the SPI interface. Non-generic, with a `name()` for registry keying and a generic `factory()` method. Implementations live anywhere on the classpath; the core package never needs to know about them.

**`AlgorithmRegistry`** (`sorting.core`) — loads all providers at class-init time via `ServiceLoader.load(SortAlgorithmProvider.class)`, which scans every `META-INF/services/sorting.core.SortAlgorithmProvider` file on the classpath. Supports programmatic `register()` as an escape hatch for runtime additions or tests.

**`META-INF/services/sorting.core.SortAlgorithmProvider`** — the ServiceLoader configuration file. Adding a new algorithm drops to two steps: write the implementation, add its provider class name here. No other files change.

**`MergeSortProvider`** (`sorting.algorithm`) — the bridge. Returns `c -> new MergeSort<>(c)` as the factory; the lambda is type-safe without unchecked casts because `c` is already `Comparator<T>`.

**`Builder.algorithm(String)`** — delegates to `AlgorithmRegistry.get(name)`, resolving at build time so a missing algorithm fails fast and clearly.

**`merge_sort.java`** — now imports only `sorting.core`. It has zero knowledge of `MergeSort` or any other algorithm; swapping to a different algorithm at runtime requires only changing the string `"merge"`.
